performance.title: Performance
performance.description: How fast the page loads and becomes interactive to users.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: How well the page accommodates users with disabilities.

best-practices.title: Best Practices
best-practices.description: Whether the page follows web development best practices.

seo.title: SEO
seo.description: How well the page is optimized for search engines.

pwa.title: Progressive Web App
pwa.description: How well the page works as a progressive web app.

first-contentful-paint.title: First Contentful Paint
first-contentful-paint.description: First Contentful Paint marks the time at which the first text or image is painted.
first-contentful-paint.warningHeader: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this.
first-contentful-paint.explanation: Fast page loads start with a quick time to the first byte (TTFB). Consider using a CDN or improving your server response times.

largest-contentful-paint.title: Largest Contentful Paint
largest-contentful-paint.description: Largest Contentful Paint marks the time at which the largest text or image is painted.
largest-contentful-paint.warningHeader: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this.
largest-contentful-paint.explanation:
To improve LCP, consider:
1. Optimizing your server response time
2. Optimizing your CSS
3. Eliminating render-blocking resources
4. Optimizing your images

speed-index.title: Speed Index
speed-index.description: Speed Index shows how quickly the contents of a page are visibly populated.

total-blocking-time.title: Total Blocking Time
total-blocking-time.description: Sum of all time periods between FCP and Time to Interactive, when task length exceeded 50ms, expressed in milliseconds.

cumulative-layout-shift.title: Cumulative Layout Shift
cumulative-layout-shift.description: Cumulative Layout Shift measures the movement of visible elements within the viewport.

interactive.title: Time to Interactive
interactive.description: Time to interactive is the amount of time it takes for the page to become fully interactive.

max-potential-fid.title: Max Potential First Input Delay
max-potential-fid.description: The maximum possible First Input Delay that users could experience.

accesskeys.title: [accesskey] values are unique
accesskeys.description: Access keys let users quickly focus a part of the page. For proper navigation, each access key must be unique.

aria-allowed-attr.title: ARIA attributes are not prohibited on an element
aria-allowed-attr.description: An aria-\* attribute on an element does not match the name of any ARIA attribute.

aria-hidden-body.title: The [aria-hidden="true"] attribute is not present on the body
aria-hidden-body.description: Assistive technology, like screen readers, work better when they only encounter text meant to be read.

aria-hidden-focus.title: Elements with aria-hidden="true" do not contain focusable elements
aria-hidden-focus.description: If elements are decorated with aria-hidden="true", ensure that neither the element nor any of its focusable descendants are unintentionally visible to screen readers.

aria-required-attr.title: ARIA states and properties have the correct values
aria-required-attr.description: Values must be valid for the given ARIA state or property.

aria-required-children.title: Elements with ARIA roles require specific children
aria-required-children.description: ARIA roles require specific attributes and children to perform their intended accessibility functions.

aria-required-parent.title: Elements with ARIA roles require specific parents
aria-required-parent.description: ARIA roles require specific parents to perform their intended accessibility functions.

aria-roles.title: ARIA roles are used correctly
aria-roles.description: ARIA roles must be used on elements that match the implicit (or explicit) role of that element.

aria-toggle-field-has-aria-checked.title: Toggle fields have a non-empty "aria-checked" state
aria-toggle-field-has-aria-checked.description: Toggle fields must have a "aria-checked" attribute that reflects the current state of the toggle.

aria-valid-attr-value.title: ARIA attributes have valid values
aria-valid-attr-value.description: All ARIA state and properties are receiving the correct values.

aria-visibility.title: ARIA hidden elements do not have focusable descendants
aria-visibility.description: When an element is hidden using aria-hidden="true", assistive technologies such as screen readers are able to ignore the element and all of its descendants.

button-name.title: Buttons have an accessible name
button-name.description: When a button doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it as "button", which is useless to a user who relies on screen readers.

color-contrast.title: Color contrast
color-contrast.description: Users who have low vision or are color deficient rely on sufficient color contrast between text and its background.

definition-list.title: Definition list items are arranged in proper order
definition-list.description: When a definition list is not properly formatted, screen readers will produce confusing output.

dlitem.title: `<dd>` elements in `<description>` must be paired
dlitem.description: In a description list, each `<dd>` element must be paired with a `<dt>` element.

document-title.title: Document title
document-title.description: Screen readers rely on a page title to inform users which page they are on.

duplicate-id.title: Duplicate ID
duplicate-id.description: As a best practice, IDs are unique. If an element’s ID is not unique, it’s not only wasted bytes: screen readers may make it harder for users to distinguish between different elements.

focus-trap.title: Users can be trapped in modal dialogs if focus is not managed properly
focus-trap.description: When a modal dialog is displayed, keyboard users may find themselves unable to exit the modal if they tab to the last focusable element within the modal.

focusable-controls.title: All form controls have associated labels
focusable-controls.description: Ensuring that labels and form controls are properly associated is critical to form accessibility.

focus-order.title: Logical tab order
focus-order.description: Tab navigation follows the order that elements are defined in the DOM.

form-field-multiple-labels.title: Form fields have only one label
form-field-multiple-labels.description: Each form field should have no more than one label.

frame-title.title: iframe elements have titles
frame-title.description: Screen­reader users rely on frame titles to describe the contents of frames.

heading-order.title: Heading levels are only descended by one
heading-order.description: Heading elements should be ordered properly. E.g. H2 – H4 is not a valid sequencing since it skips H3.

html-has-lang.title: html element has a [lang] attribute
html-has-lang.description: If a page doesn’t specify a lang attribute, a screen reader assumes that the page is in the default language that the user chose when setting up the screen reader.

html-lang-valid.title: html[lang] attribute is valid
html-lang-valid.description: One of the most common causes of an invalid language value is incorrectly copying and pasting language codes.

image-alt.title: Image elements have [alt] attributes
image-alt.description: Informative elements should aim for short, descriptive alternate text. Decorative elements can be ignored by screen readers.

input-image-alt.title: Image buttons have [alt] attributes
input-image-alt.description: If an input element has an image as the source, then it must specify an alternate text.

label.title: Form elements have associated labels
label.description: Ensuring that labels and form controls are properly associated is critical to form accessibility.

layout-table.title: Tables are not being used for layout
layout-table.description: Using tables for layout presents several accessibility concerns to users who rely on screen readers.

link-name.title: Links have a discernible name
link-name.description: The link text (and alternate text for images, if present) is discernible by screen readers.

list.title: List items are not contained in <li> elements
list.description: List items must be contained in <li> elements to be accessible to screen readers.

listitem.title: List items are properly spaced
listitem.description: List items must have adequate vertical spacing to be legible.

logical-tab-order.title: Logical tab order
logical-tab-order.description: Custom keyboard navigation controls need to follow a logical tab order.

meta-viewport.title: Document has a meta viewport
meta-viewport.description: The meta viewport element gives browser instructions on how to control the page’s dimensions and scaling.

object-alt.title: Objects have alternative text
object-alt.description: Screen readers cannot translate non-text content. Adding alternative text helps convey the purpose of non-text objects in web pages.

rotation.title: User can adjust the text spacing
rotation.description: Ensure that line height (leading), tracking, and word spacing can be adjusted without loss of content or function.

skip-heading.title: Skipping heading levels
skip-heading.description: Skipping heading levels can be confusing and should be avoided where possible.

splash-screen.title: Does not delay the first paint
splash-screen.description: Pages that have a splash screen or an app install banner delay the first paint.

tabindex.title: Tabindex attributes are used correctly
tabindex.description: tabIndex must be greater than or equal to 0.

touchevent-listeners.title: Touch event listeners
touchevent-listeners.description: Applications that listen to touch events on elements must do so explicitly rather than relying on mouse events.

video-caption.title: Video elements have captions
video-caption.description: Video captions make videos accessible to people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

video-description.title: Video elements have descriptions
video-description.description: Video descriptions make videos accessible to people who are blind or have low vision.

manifest-exists.title: Web App Manifest Exists
manifest-exists.description: Web App Manifests make your web application usable offline and provide a native-like experience.

manifest-start-url.title: Manifest start_url is safe to use
manifest-start-url.description: The start_url is required and should be preferably pointing to index.html.

uses-http2.title: Uses HTTP/2
uses-http2.description: Using HTTP/2 can offer many benefits over HTTP/1.x, including better performance.

uses-long-cache-ttl.title: Uses long cache TTL
uses-long-cache-ttl.description: Leveraging the browser cache can speed up page loads by reducing network latency.

uses-rel-preconnect.title: Uses preconnect to reduce request latency
uses-rel-preconnect.description: Preconnect hints tell the browser to initiate an early connection to an origin.

uses-rel-preload.title: Uses preload to optimize key requests
uses-rel-preload.description: Preload hints tell the browser to request critical resources ahead of time.

uses-rel-prerender.title: Uses prerender to reduce request latency
uses-rel-prerender.description: Prerender hints tell the browser to render a page in advance.

redirects.title: Avoids an excessive number of redirects
redirects.description: Having more than one redirect is unnecessary. In the worst case, each redirect incurs an additional network round-trip, which adds delay to the overall request.

uses-text-compression.title: Enable Text Compression
uses-text-compression.description: Text-based resources should be served with compression (gzip, deflate or brotli) to minimize total network bytes.

offline-start-url.title: Start_url responds with a 200 when offline
offline-start-url.description: If you specify a start_url in your manifest, it should respond with a 200 when the user is offline.

redirects-http.title: Redirects HTTP traffic to HTTPS
redirects-http.description: If you have already set up your website to use HTTPS, make sure that you redirect all HTTP traffic to that secure version.

is-on-https.title: Is on HTTPS
is-on-https.description: Secure websites have URLs that begin with https:// rather than http://.

geolocation-on-start.title: Does not request the geolocation permission on entry
geolocation-on-start.description: Sites that immediately request geolocation upon page load can appear untrustworthy before the user gets the chance to navigate away from the site.

notification-on-start.title: Does not request the notification permission on entry
notification-on-start.description: Sites that immediately request notifications upon page load can appear untrustworthy before the user gets the chance to navigate away from the site.

device-forgetful-user.title: Is not vulnerable to the fortnite bug
device-forgetful-user.description: Ensure that the site is not vulnerable to the "Fortnite bug" where allowing access to specific sensors can lead to leaking of sensitive data.

json-valid-schema.title: Manifest is a valid JSON
json-valid-schema.description: While parsing the manifest, it is possible to encounter an error. Validate your manifest against the official schema to ensure it is valid.

csp-xss.title: Content Security Policy (CSP): XSS protection
csp-xss.description: This audit checks whether your CSP is effective against XSS attacks.

efficient-animated-content.title: Uses efficient animated content
efficient-animated-content.description: Consider using CSS transitions instead of JavaScript animations to create performant animations.

bootup-time.title: JavaScript bootup time is high
bootup-time.description: High bootup time indicates a large amount of JavaScript is being parsed and/or compiled on the main thread.

double-zoom.title: Page isn't be zoom is disabled
double-zoom.description: This test ensures that there are no user-scalable=no values in the viewport meta tag.

critical-request-chains.title: Reduce the impact of third-party code
critical-request-chains.description: Third-party code can significantly impact load performance. Limit the number of redundant third-party providers and try to load third-party code after your main content has loaded.

render-blocking-resources.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
render-blocking-resources.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles.

unused-css-rules.title: Reduce unused CSS
unused-css-rules.description: If the page uses excessive amounts of CSS, much of it may be unnecessary.

unused-javascript.title: Remove unused JavaScript
unused-javascript.description: Users today are blessed with prolific amounts of JavaScript in their journey to building whatever they dream of.

uses-responsive-images.title: Serve images with appropriate dimensions
uses-responsive-images.description: Your page might be using images that are larger than they need to be on the user's device.

total-byte-weight.title: Total Byte Weight
total-byte-weight.description: Total byte weight for HTML + JS + CSS + Images

uses-webp-images.title: Use image formats better suited for the web
uses-webp-images.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption.

unminified-javascript.title: Minify JavaScript
unminified-javascript.description: JavaScript files that are not minified are unnecessarily large.

unused-css-rules.title: Reduce unused CSS from third-party providers
unused-css-rules.description: If you use a third-party library, it's possible that some of the CSS you are including is not required for your specific use case.
